Review of the working tree (step 4, uncommitted, on top of 84466639d) against specs/07_09_22_31_PAT_tokens_spec.md sections 4.1, 4.2, 8.3

Round 1 for step 4 (authentication transports and find_current_user).

Verdict

APPROVE. No blocking findings. The controller branch and the Doorkeeper configuration match the spec text line for line, all fourteen spec-listed integration tests exist and pass, the wider API suite is green, and every acceptance criterion reachable without the UI was confirmed live against the Docker server with a freshly minted admin token. Findings are documentation and test-coverage nits.

Acceptance criteria

# Criterion Status Evidence
5 Bearer → 200 Met Live 200; test_should_accept_pat_as_bearer_token.
6 X-Redmine-API-Key → 200 Met Live 200; test.
7 ?key= → 200 and [FILTERED] in log Met Live 200; plaintext occurs zero times in log/development.log.
8 Basic username → 200 Met Live 200; test.
9 Admin PAT on /users.json → 200 Met Live 200; api_key present in the owner's /users/current.json, proving OAuth-scoped mode is off.
10 Last used after a request Met at data level last_used_at set live and in test; the "used less than a minute ago" text is step 6.
11 Revoked → 401 Bearer invalid_token Met at API level test_should_deny_revoked_pat; list behaviour is step 6.
12 Expired → 401 Bearer Met at API level Live, on Bearer and on ?key=: WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="Redmine", error="invalid_token", error_description="The access token expired".
13 Legacy key unchanged Met test_legacy_api_key_should_still_work_on_every_transport; live 200 with the admin's legacy key; _sidebar.html.erb untouched.
16 RuboCop clean Met 3 files, no offenses. zeitwerk:check not rerun this round; no constant was added.
18 Nothing out of scope Met

Blocking findings

None.

Non-blocking findings

R-19. Unknown-token test asserts the challenge header on three of five transports.

  • Where: test_should_deny_unknown_token_on_every_transport, the two query-parameter cases at the end.
  • Problem: they assert only :unauthorized. The header transports also assert Basic realm="Redmine API". Symmetry costs two lines and would catch a future change that routes ?key= through Doorkeeper's error path.

R-20. X-Redmine-Switch-User with a PAT has no test.

  • Where: spec 4.2 says the switch "still applies afterwards"; no test in 8.3 either, so this is not a spec gap on the implementer's side.
  • Problem: the code path is unchanged, but its input changed: user.admin? is now true for a full-access PAT because oauth_scope stays nil. One test with an admin PAT and the header would pin that. I could not check it live because the Docker database has only the admin user.

R-21. Two behaviour changes need explicit README wording, not just spec mentions.

  • A request carrying an invalid legacy key in X-Redmine-API-Key or ?key= plus valid Basic username and password now authenticates through Basic. In 6.1.2 the invalid key short-circuited to 401. Spec 4.2 says this; the README "important items" list should too, since it is what a maintainer will ask about.
  • The 401 challenge tells the caller whether a token is real but dead (Bearer ... invalid_token with "expired" or "revoked" in the description) or unknown (Basic realm). This is Doorkeeper's existing behaviour for OAuth tokens, now reachable with PATs on the legacy transports. Spec 4.2 records it as a known difference; the README limits section should say plainly that it discloses token liveness.

R-22. The locked-user crash is still in upstream trunk.

  • Where: ai-workflow/architecture.md 1.3.1, new bullet.
  • I confirmed the claim: both tag 6.1.4 and current master still do user.oauth_scope = ... with no nil guard after User.active.find_by_id. So this fix is ours, not a backport, and is a candidate for an upstream ticket. Worth saying in the README so a maintainer sees it as a contribution rather than a drive-by change.

Lens-by-lens summary

  • Spec conformance. access_token_methods in config/initializers/30-redmine.rb:52-57 matches spec 4.1 exactly, including order. The API branch in app/controllers/application_controller.rb:131-142 matches spec 4.2 exactly. All fourteen 8.3 tests present, plus one useful extra: a scoped application token on the admin endpoint gets 403, pinning that the full_access? split did not loosen OAuth-flow tokens.
  • Correctness, traced. Doorkeeper's from_request (oauth/token.rb:7-13) accepts symbols and callables and stops at the first present? value, so the .presence in the two lambdas is what makes them fall through cleanly. Live paths: real token on five transports 200; expired 401 Bearer; revoked 401 Bearer (test); unknown 401 Basic realm; locked owner 401 not 500 (test, and the implementer reproduced the 500 with the guard stashed); legacy key 200; no credentials 401. Doorkeeper.authenticate also calls revoke_previous_refresh_token! on every hit, but the mixin returns early when previous_refresh_token is blank (l.435), and the log shows exactly one UPDATE ... SET last_used_at per request and nothing else.
  • Security. No plaintext in the log on any transport. The username of an ordinary Basic login now gets hashed and looked up once; the result is nil and nothing is disclosed. Full-access detection requires both no application and no scopes, so a future scoped PAT is enforced automatically. The PAT is consumed before the Basic branch, so the 2FA and must_change_password? checks there do not apply; that is D-021 and is documented. One pre-existing fact worth knowing: actions declared accept_api_auth also accept keys on HTML requests. GET /my/account renders "Logged in as admin" with a legacy key today, and now with a PAT as well. Parity, not a regression; CSRF still applies to HTML POSTs because Redmine only skips it for XML and JSON. The step 6 controller must not declare accept_api_auth, which spec 5.2 already forbids.
  • Redmine conventions. Rocket hashes, lambda {|request| ...} in Redmine's block style, comments in the initializer mirror the surrounding ones. The empty if body with a comment is accepted by RuboCop and reads clearly.
  • Tests. Redmine::ApiTest::Base, require_relative at the right depth, def test_..., credentials helper, with_settings, teardown resets User.current. Assertions on status, challenge header and returned login, not on internals. Every failure path in the spec has a case.
  • Backward compatibility. Whole test/integration/api_test/ directory, account and sudo-mode suites green. Two intentional behaviour changes listed under R-21.
  • Documentation. Architecture 2.4 and the new 1.3.1 bullet are accurate. Line pointers verified.
  • Diff hygiene. git diff --check clean. No debug code. Temporary tokens I created for the live check were deleted.

Notes for the human's final review

+    redmine_default = [
+      :"field_#{class_prefix}_#{prepared_attr}",
+      :"field_#{prepared_attr}"
+    ]
+    options[:default] = redmine_default + Array(options[:default])
+    super
+  end
+
   # Lifetimes an owner may choose, capped by the admin setting (0 = no cap)
   def self.allowed_lifetimes
     cap = Setting.personal_access_token_max_lifetime.to_i

# along with this program; if not, write to the Free Software
# Foundation, Inc., 51 Franklin Street, Fifth Floor, Boston, MA  02110-1301, USA.

class PersonalAccessTokensController < ApplicationController
  self.main_menu = false

  # Declared first: the one-time plaintext travels in the flash for a single
  # redirect and must be consumed before any later filter can render a page
  # that would print it as a flash message
  before_action :read_new_token_from_flash
  before_action :require_login
  before_action :require_rest_api_enabled
  before_action :find_token, :only => :destroy
  require_sudo_mode :create, :destroy

  def index
    @tokens = User.current.personal_access_tokens.not_revoked.order(:created_at => :desc).to_a
    @token ||= PersonalAccessToken.new
    no_store if @new_token_value
  end

  def create
    @token = PersonalAccessToken.new(:user => User.current)
    @token.safe_attributes = params[:personal_access_token]
    if @token.save
      flash[:personal_access_token] = [@token.plaintext_token]
      flash[:notice] = l(:notice_personal_access_token_created)
      redirect_to my_api_tokens_path
    else
      index
      render :action => 'index'
    end
  end

  def destroy
    @token.revoke
    flash[:notice] = l(:notice_personal_access_token_revoked)
    redirect_to my_api_tokens_path
  end

  private

  def read_new_token_from_flash
    @new_token_value = Array(flash[:personal_access_token]).first
    flash.delete(:personal_access_token)
  end

  def require_rest_api_enabled
    deny_access unless Setting.rest_api_enabled?
  end

  # Revoked tokens are not listed, so they are not found either
  def find_token
    @token = User.current.personal_access_tokens.not_revoked.find(params[:id])
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    render_404
  end
end

require_relative '../test_helper'

class PersonalAccessTokensControllerTest < Redmine::ControllerTest
  def setup
    User.current = nil
    @request.session[:user_id] = 2
    Setting.rest_api_enabled = '1'
  end

  def teardown
    Setting.rest_api_enabled = '0'
  end

  def test_index_should_list_active_and_expired_but_not_revoked_tokens
    active = PersonalAccessToken.generate!(:name => 'Active one')
    expired = PersonalAccessToken.generate!(:name => 'Expired one', :lifetime_days => 7)
    expired.update_column(:created_at, 8.days.ago)
    revoked = PersonalAccessToken.generate!(:name => 'Revoked one')
    revoked.revoke

    get :index
    assert_response :success
    assert_select 'table.personal-access-tokens tbody tr', 2
    assert_select "tr#personal-access-token-#{active.id}" do
      assert_select 'td.name', :text => 'Active one'
      assert_select 'td code', :text => "…#{active.token_suffix}"
      assert_select 'td.status', :text => 'Active'
      assert_select 'a[href=?][data-method=delete]', "/my/api_tokens/#{active.id}"
    end
    assert_select "tr#personal-access-token-#{expired.id} td.status", :text => 'Expired'
    assert_select "tr#personal-access-token-#{revoked.id}", 0
    assert_select 'pre#new-personal-access-token', 0
  end

  def test_index_without_tokens_should_show_nodata
    get :index
    assert_response :success
    assert_select 'table.personal-access-tokens', 0
    assert_select 'p.nodata'
  end

  def test_index_should_show_last_used
    token = PersonalAccessToken.generate!
    get :index
    assert_select "tr#personal-access-token-#{token.id} td", :text => 'Never'

    token.update_column(:last_used_at, 3.hours.ago)
    get :index
    assert_select "tr#personal-access-token-#{token.id} td", :text => 'used about 3 hours ago'
  end

  def test_index_should_render_legacy_api_key_sidebar
    get :index
    assert_select '#sidebar pre#api-access-key'
  end

  def test_index_should_require_login
    @request.session[:user_id] = nil
    get :index
    assert_redirected_to '/login?back_url=http%3A%2F%2Ftest.host%2Fmy%2Fapi_tokens'
  end

  def test_index_should_deny_when_rest_api_disabled
    Setting.rest_api_enabled = '0'
    get :index
    assert_response :forbidden
  end

  def test_index_should_show_create_form_with_allowed_lifetimes
    get :index
    assert_response :success
    assert_select 'form[action="/my/api_tokens"]' do
      assert_select 'input[name=?]', 'personal_access_token[name]'
      assert_select 'label[for=personal_access_token_name] span.required'
      assert_select 'label[for=personal_access_token_lifetime_days]', :text => /Expires in/
      assert_select 'select[name=?]', 'personal_access_token[lifetime_days]' do
        assert_select 'option', 6
        assert_select 'option[value="30"][selected=selected]', :text => '30 days'
      end
    end
  end

  def test_index_should_show_create_form_with_cap
    with_settings :personal_access_token_max_lifetime => 30 do
      get :index
      assert_select 'select[name=?]', 'personal_access_token[lifetime_days]' do
        assert_select 'option', 2
        assert_select 'option[value="7"]'
        assert_select 'option[value="30"][selected=selected]'
      end
    end
    with_settings :personal_access_token_max_lifetime => 7 do
      get :index
      assert_select 'select[name=?]', 'personal_access_token[lifetime_days]' do
        assert_select 'option', 1
        assert_select 'option[value="7"][selected=selected]'
      end
    end
  end

  def test_index_should_show_create_form_without_form_when_no_lifetime_allowed
    with_settings :personal_access_token_max_lifetime => 3 do
      get :index
      assert_response :success
      assert_select 'form[action="/my/api_tokens"]', 0
      assert_select 'p.warning', :text => 'No token lifetime is allowed by the administrator.'
    end
  end

  def test_create_should_create_token_and_show_plaintext_once
    assert_difference 'PersonalAccessToken.count' do
      post :create, :params => {:personal_access_token => {:name => 'CI job', :lifetime_days => '60'}}
    end
    assert_redirected_to '/my/api_tokens'
    token = PersonalAccessToken.personal.order(:id).last
    assert_equal 'CI job', token.name
    assert_equal 60.days.to_i, token.expires_in
    assert_equal 2, token.resource_owner_id

    get :index
    assert_response :success
    assert_includes @response.headers['Cache-Control'], 'no-store'
    assert_select 'pre#new-personal-access-token' do |pre|
      plaintext = pre.text.strip
      assert plaintext.start_with?('rmpat_')
      assert_equal token.id, Doorkeeper::AccessToken.by_token(plaintext).id
    end
    assert_select 'div.flash.notice', :text => /Copy it now/

    get :index
    assert_response :success
    assert_select 'pre#new-personal-access-token', 0
    assert_not_includes @response.headers['Cache-Control'].to_s, 'no-store'
  end

  def test_new_token_should_never_be_rendered_as_flash_message
    post :create, :params => {:personal_access_token => {:name => 'CI job', :lifetime_days => '30'}}
    get :index
    assert_response :success
    assert_select '#flash_personal_access_token', 0
    assert_select 'pre#new-personal-access-token', 1

    Setting.rest_api_enabled = '0'
    get :index, :flash => {:personal_access_token => ['rmpat_secretsecretsecretsecretsecretsecretsec']}
    assert_response :forbidden
    assert_select '#flash_personal_access_token', 0
    assert_not_includes @response.body, 'rmpat_secret'
  end

  def test_create_with_invalid_name_should_rerender_form
    assert_no_difference 'PersonalAccessToken.count' do
      post :create, :params => {:personal_access_token => {:name => '', :lifetime_days => '30'}}
    end
    assert_response :success
    assert_select_error /Name cannot be blank/
    assert_select 'select[name=?] option[value="30"][selected=selected]', 'personal_access_token[lifetime_days]'
  end

  def test_create_with_lifetime_above_cap_should_fail
    with_settings :personal_access_token_max_lifetime => 30 do
      assert_no_difference 'PersonalAccessToken.count' do
        post :create, :params => {:personal_access_token => {:name => 'CI job', :lifetime_days => '90'}}
      end
      assert_response :success
      assert_select_error /Expires in is not included in the list/
    end
  end

  def test_create_with_duplicate_name_should_fail
    PersonalAccessToken.generate!(:name => 'CI job')
    assert_no_difference 'PersonalAccessToken.count' do
      post :create, :params => {:personal_access_token => {:name => 'ci JOB', :lifetime_days => '30'}}
    end
    assert_response :success
    assert_select_error /Name has already been taken/
  end

  def test_create_should_ignore_unsafe_attributes
    application = Doorkeeper::Application.create!(
      :name => 'Test app', :redirect_uri => 'https://example.com/callback', :scopes => 'admin'
    )
    post :create, :params => {
      :personal_access_token => {
        :name => 'CI job', :lifetime_days => '30',
        :expires_in => 10.years.to_i, :scopes => 'admin',
        :application_id => application.id, :resource_owner_id => 1
      }
    }
    assert_redirected_to '/my/api_tokens'
    token = PersonalAccessToken.personal.order(:id).last
    assert_equal 30.days.to_i, token.expires_in
    assert token.scopes.all.empty?
    assert_nil token.application_id
    assert_equal 2, token.resource_owner_id
  end

  def test_destroy_should_revoke_token
    token = PersonalAccessToken.generate!
    assert_no_difference 'Doorkeeper::AccessToken.count' do
      delete :destroy, :params => {:id => token.id}
    end
    assert_redirected_to '/my/api_tokens'
    assert_not_nil token.reload.revoked_at
    assert_equal 'Personal access token revoked.', flash[:notice]
  end

  def test_destroy_should_not_revoke_other_users_token
    token = PersonalAccessToken.generate!(:user => User.find(3))
    delete :destroy, :params => {:id => token.id}
    assert_response :not_found
    assert_nil token.reload.revoked_at
  end

  def test_destroy_of_already_revoked_token_should_be_not_found
    token = PersonalAccessToken.generate!
    token.revoke
    delete :destroy, :params => {:id => token.id}
    assert_response :not_found
  end

  def test_destroy_should_deny_when_rest_api_disabled
    token = PersonalAccessToken.generate!
    Setting.rest_api_enabled = '0'
    delete :destroy, :params => {:id => token.id}
    assert_response :forbidden
    assert_nil token.reload.revoked_at
  end
end

+- How the page works: `index` lists the owner's non-revoked tokens (expired ones
+  stay listed, marked "Expired", until revoked, D-014) with name, the last four
+  characters of the token, created, expires, last used ("used N ago" or "Never"),
+  status and a Revoke link (`delete_link`, confirm dialog built in). Below it a
+  `labelled_form_for` create form with name and the lifetime picker built from
+  `PersonalAccessToken.allowed_lifetimes`, 30 days preselected when allowed (D-006,
+  D-017); when the admin cap allows nothing, a warning replaces the form. The My
+  account sidebar partial is rendered as on the authorized-applications page, so
+  the legacy API key block is there unchanged (D-005).
+- How the plaintext is shown once (D-007, D-022): `create` saves, puts
+  `[plaintext]` (an Array) in `flash[:personal_access_token]` and redirects. The
+  controller's first `before_action`, `read_new_token_from_flash`, runs before
+  `require_login`, the REST API gate and sudo mode: it unwraps the value into
+  `@new_token_value` and deletes the flash key. `index` then renders a `div.box`
+  with the plaintext in `pre#new-personal-access-token`, the sidebar's copy button
+  markup (`data-controller="api-key-copy"`, reused as is) and sends
+  `Cache-Control: no-store`. The next request has no flash, so the list shows the
+  notice only. The Array wrapping means the layout's `render_flash_messages`, which
+  prints only String flash values, can never print the token even if an error page
+  is rendered before the callback; both cases are tested
+  (`test_new_token_should_never_be_rendered_as_flash_message`).
+- Access rules: `require_login`; 403 when the REST API is disabled
+  (`deny_access`); `require_sudo_mode :create, :destroy` (the confirmation page
+  keeps the posted fields as hidden inputs and re-posts them, tested end to end in
+  `sudo_mode_test.rb`); `destroy` finds only the current user's non-revoked tokens
+  and answers 404 otherwise, so revoked tokens behave as if gone (C-8); no
+  `accept_api_auth`, so a token cannot manage tokens. Mass assignment goes through
+  `safe_attributes` (`name`, `lifetime_days` only), tested with a POST that also
+  sends `expires_in`, `scopes`, `application_id` and `resource_owner_id`.

- `read_new_token_from_flash` (**declared first**): reads
  `flash[:personal_access_token]` into `@new_token_value` (unwrapping the Array), then
  deletes the key, on every action. Two statements: `FlashHash#delete` returns the
  hash, not the value (C-15). Reason (C-2):
  `render_flash_messages` (`application_helper.rb:516-524`) prints every String flash
  value on any page, including a 403 or 500 error page that has no `no_store`. The six
  `ApplicationController` callbacks (`application_controller.rb:64`) run before this
  one but only redirect; every later failure point (login, REST API gate, sudo mode,
  exceptions) runs after the flash was consumed. Belt and braces: `create` stores the
  value wrapped in an Array (`flash[:personal_access_token] = [plaintext]`), which the
  `is_a?(String)` guard in `render_flash_messages` skips by construction, exactly as
  the backup codes store an Array of ids. The callback unwraps it.
- `require_rest_api_enabled`: `deny_access unless Setting.rest_api_enabled?`
  (`deny_access` → 403 for a logged-in user, l.317). Same gate as the Doorkeeper
  screens and the sidebar key block.
- `index`: `@tokens = User.current.personal_access_tokens.not_revoked.order(:created_at => :desc).to_a`;
  `@token ||= PersonalAccessToken.new`; `no_store if @new_token_value`.
- `create`: `@token = PersonalAccessToken.new(:user => User.current)`;
  `@token.safe_attributes = params[:personal_access_token]`; on `save`:
  `flash[:personal_access_token] = [@token.plaintext_token]`,
  `flash[:notice] = l(:notice_personal_access_token_created)`,
  `redirect_to my_api_tokens_path`. On failure: `index` then `render :action => 'index'`
  (pattern of `EmailAddressesController#create`, l.42-46).
- Flash messages are rendered with `html_safe` (C-10): every flash string in this
  controller is a static `l(:key)`; never interpolate the token name or any other user
  input into a flash message.
- Known UX limit (C-2, README): if the session expires between the POST and the
  redirected GET, `require_login` redirects without keeping the flash and the plaintext
  is lost; the user revokes and recreates. No code for this.
- Known development-only limit (C-14, README): Rails' debug error page renders a
  "session dump" (`actionpack .../rescues/_request_and_response.html.erb:7-8`), and
  the session still holds the previous request's flash until the action finishes.
  An exception on the redirected GET therefore shows the plaintext there, but only
  when `consider_all_requests_local` is true, i.e. development and test
  (`config/environments/development.rb:17`); production renders a static page. No
  code for this.
- `destroy`: `token = User.current.personal_access_tokens.not_revoked.find(params[:id])`
  (404 for another user's id or for an already revoked one, consistent with revoked
  tokens not being listed; C-8); `token.revoke`; flash
  `notice_personal_access_token_revoked`; `redirect_to my_api_tokens_path`.
- No `accept_api_auth`: this page is session-only (a token must not manage tokens).

*`require_sudo_mode` re-asks the password for these actions when an admin enabled
sudo mode in `configuration.yml`; it is a no-op otherwise and in tests (`arch 1.4`).*

# Foundation, Inc., 51 Franklin Street, Fifth Floor, Boston, MA  02110-1301, USA.
class ApplicationRecord < ActiveRecord::Base
  self.abstract_class = true

  # Translate attribute names for validation errors display
  def self.human_attribute_name(attr, options = {})
    prepared_attr = attr.to_s.sub(/_id$/, '').sub(/^.+\./, '')
    class_prefix = name.underscore.tr('/', '_')
    redmine_default = [
      :"field_#{class_prefix}_#{prepared_attr}",
      :"field_#{prepared_attr}"
    ]
    options[:default] = redmine_default + Array(options[:default])
    super
  end
end

    const apiKeyText = this.apiKeyTarget.textContent?.trim();
    if (!apiKeyText) return;

    const svgIcon = event.target.closest('.copy-api-key-link').querySelector('svg')
    if (!svgIcon) return;

    copyToClipboard(apiKeyText).then(() => {
      updateSVGIcon(svgIcon, 'checked');
      setTimeout(() => {
        updateSVGIcon(svgIcon, 'copy');
      }, 2000);
    });
  }

Blocking findings

None.

Non-blocking findings

R-25. PersonalAccessToken.human_attribute_name duplicates fourteen lines of ApplicationRecord.

  • Where: app/models/personal_access_token.rb:65-78; origin app/models/application_record.rb:23-33.
  • Problem: necessary, because Doorkeeper::AccessToken inherits from ActiveRecord::Base and skips Redmine's field_<attr> label lookup, so without it the error reads "Lifetime days is not included in the list". Three other Redmine models override the same method for their own reasons, so the shape is not foreign. But the copy is verbatim and will drift silently if ApplicationRecord changes.
  • Suggested handling: this is a design choice the spec did not anticipate, so it needs a D-NNN. The implementer proposed one. The alternatives worth recording: extract the body of ApplicationRecord.human_attribute_name into a small module and include it in both places (touches core, cleaner), or keep the copy with a comment pointing at the source (what is there now). Either is defensible; the README should say which and why.

R-26. destroy resolves the token before the sudo-mode prompt.

  • Where: before_action :find_token, :only => :destroy is declared before require_sudo_mode, so its filter runs first.
  • Problem: a DELETE for a foreign or revoked id answers 404 without asking for the password; a valid id gets the prompt. Spec 5.2 placed the lookup inside the action, after sudo. No security impact: only the caller's own tokens can be found, and their ids are on the page. Mentioning it because it is an unstated deviation; architecture 2.6 lists the filter but not the order.

Lens-by-lens summary

  • Spec conformance. Routes, controller callbacks, index, create, destroy, view sections 1 to 6, the My account link and all sixteen locale keys match the spec. Every test in 8.4, 8.4a, 8.5 and 8.7 is present, plus five useful extras (empty state, last-used text, sidebar key block present, revoked id 404, destroy when REST API disabled). Deviations, all documented in architecture 2.6: the human_attribute_name override (R-25), :required passed to the form builder's options rather than HTML options (correct for Redmine's LabelledFormBuilder), and the find_token filter (R-26).
  • Correctness. The flash path is right: read_new_token_from_flash is the first callback, unwraps with Array(...).first, then deletes the key in a second statement (C-15). create stores an Array, so the layout's render_flash_messages (application_helper.rb:519, next unless v.is_a?(String)) cannot print it. no_store only on the display request. index is reused for the failure re-render so the list stays populated. The preselect logic keeps the user's choice on validation failure and falls back to 30 or the first allowed value.
  • Security. require_login, REST API gate via deny_access, sudo mode on both mutating actions with the posted fields carried through the confirmation page (tested end to end). No accept_api_auth, so a token cannot manage tokens. safe_attributes limits mass assignment; the unsafe-attributes test posts expires_in, scopes, application_id and resource_owner_id and proves all are ignored. Ownership is enforced in the query, not by a check after loading. All flash strings are static l(:key). ERB escapes the token name. delete_link carries the CSRF token through rails-ujs. Plaintext appears zero times in the development log after the live walk.
  • Redmine conventions. GPL header and frozen literal on the controller and test; rocket hashes; self.main_menu = false as in AccountController; explicit named routes and _path helpers in the view; title breadcrumb helper; table.list shape with td.buttons and delete_link; labelled_form_for in fieldset.box.tabular; content_for :sidebar with the my/sidebar partial exactly as the authorized-applications page; html_title; keys under the right prefixes, English only.
  • Tests. Redmine::ControllerTest, session set in setup, Setting.rest_api_enabled toggled and restored, assert_select with name=? placeholders, assert_select_error, assert_difference. The sudo test uses expire_sudo_mode! after log_user as C-7 required. Assertions are on rendered HTML and database state.
  • Backward compatibility. _sidebar.html.erb untouched; My account gains one link; EmailAddressesController and TwofaController suites green.
  • Documentation. Architecture 1.9 finding and 2.6 accurate; counts of tests and keys verified.
  • Diff hygiene. git diff --check clean. No leftovers. Throwaway users created for the live walk were deleted; none remain.

Confirmed, and it is a real gap, though a narrow one. Here is the precise picture.

What happens today. A Doorkeeper::AccessToken created outside our model with no application, no expires_in and no scopes (the one-liner a console user, a plugin or a data migration would write) is, in the current branch:

  • accessible forever: Doorkeeper's expired? is !!(expires_in && ...), so nil means never expires;
  • full access: full_access? returns true, so oauth_scope is never set and the owner's complete rights apply, including admin;
  • tracked and listed: it appears on my/api_tokens with an empty name, an empty expiry cell and status "Active", and it can be revoked there.

I created exactly such a row for the admin in a rolled-back transaction and observed all three.

Confirmed, and it is a real gap, though a narrow one. Here is the precise picture.

What happens today. A Doorkeeper::AccessToken created outside our model with no application, no expires_in and no scopes (the one-liner a console user, a plugin or a data migration would write) is, in the current branch:

  • accessible forever: Doorkeeper's expired? is !!(expires_in && ...), so nil means never expires;
  • full access: full_access? returns true, so oauth_scope is never set and the owner's complete rights apply, including admin;
  • tracked and listed: it appears on my/api_tokens with an empty name, an empty expiry cell and status "Active", and it can be revoked there.

I created exactly such a row for the admin in a rolled-back transaction and observed all three.

What 6.1.2 did with the same row. It authenticated but got oauth_scope = [], which makes admin? false and allowed_to? fail for everything. The row was a valid but useless credential. Our D-010 rule "application-less plus blank scopes equals full access" is what promotes it. So the branch changes the meaning of a data shape that already existed, and the promotion carries none of the PAT guarantees the ticket asks for: no mandatory expiry, no name, no last-four for identification.

Why it is not a vulnerability. Creating such a row requires the Rails console, a plugin, or direct database access. Anyone with those can already set the admin password, mint a legacy API key, or edit the OAuth tables directly, so no trust boundary is crossed. Doorkeeper's own flows always attach an application, so no HTTP path produces the row. The proper classification is a robustness and defensibility gap: a Redmine maintainer reading the MR will ask exactly your question, and the honest current answer is "yes, such a token becomes a never-ending full-access credential".

Proposed fix: make the full-access test require the PAT invariant, not just the absence of an application. One extra condition closes it:

def self.full_access?(access_token)
  access_token.application_id.nil? &&
    access_token.expires_in.present? &&
    access_token.scopes.all.empty?
end

Effects:

  • A genuine PAT always has expires_in, because the model derives it from the mandatory lifetime, so nothing changes for tokens created through the UI.
  • A foreign application-less token without expiry falls back to 6.1.2 behaviour: it authenticates with an empty scope and can do nothing. The "mandatory expiration" promise then holds for every full-access token in the table, whoever created it.
  • Fully backward compatible: no such token could do anything in 6.1.2 either.

A stricter variant also requires name.present?, which ties full access to "was created by our model". I would not go that far: expires_in is the property the ticket cares about, and requiring a name would punish a future admin tool that legitimately issues app-less tokens with expiry.

Two companion changes.

  1. A unit test in personal_access_token_test.rb, a fifth case in test_full_access_should_be_true_only_for_app_less_token_with_blank_scopes: an app-less token created with expires_in: nil is not full access. And an integration test: such a token on /users.xml for the admin gets 403, not 200.
  2. README limits: "Tokens inserted into oauth_access_tokens outside the UI are not personal access tokens. Without an expiry they authenticate with no scope and can do nothing, as in 6.1.2. They do appear on the token page and can be revoked there."

Optionally, scope :personal and the User#personal_access_tokens association could also exclude rows without a name so the list only shows real PATs, but listing foreign rows is arguably useful, since it lets the owner see and revoke them. I would leave the listing as is and mention it.

Process. This changes spec 3.2's definition of full_access? and touches D-010's wording, so under D-026 it goes through a planner session: a D-NNN entry recording the gap, the chosen condition and the alternatives above, then the implementer applies it in step 4's files. I would treat it as recommended before the MR rather than optional: it costs three lines and two tests, and it turns a reviewer's question into a documented design property.

I will carry it as finding R-27 in the final whole-branch review.
